authority_note: Canary promotion authority is a TEST_ONLY fixture. No real Mikko decision was fabricated; the retained lifecycle canary was not classified or moved.

baseline.evidence: Zero files across *.js, *.json and *.md for draft_mode, review_mode, production_mode, capture_mode, presenter_mode, proxy_presenter, human_presenter, synthetic_delivery, real_capture, production_tier and run_mode. The REVIEW literals that do exist are attention levels (INFORMATION | REVIEW | DECISION), an unrelated axis.
baseline.consequence: Gate 7 conflated machine preparation, proxy delivery, real human performance and take logging, so its single declared owner could only be correct for one of them.

mode_contract.no_production_to_draft: discarding a locked human performance back to proxy delivery is a new run, not a mode change

DRAFT.meaning: Proxy delivery readiness. A draft is performed by the machine, so nothing here may require Mikko to record.
required_evidence: synthetic delivery manifest (proxy presenter delivery plan)
blocked_by: no synthetic delivery artifact contract exists; presenter-take-manifest models real human delivery only (TRANSCRIPT_SOURCES HUMAN_SUPPLIED/IMPORTED/EXTERNAL_TRANSCRIPTION, FIDELITY_METHODS ... HUMAN_VERIFIED, createHumanSelection)
PRESENTER_A_ROLL is excluded from visual-plan-prompt-adapter PROMPT_MEDIA, so presenter delivery is contractually not machine-generable
no text-to-speech, avatar, or synthetic-voice producer exists anywhere in the repository

REVIEW.meaning: Entering REVIEW introduces no capture requirement. Review judges a draft that already exists; whatever capture the draft produced stands.

PRODUCTION.meaning: Machine preparation for a real recording session, then Mikko's actual performance. The two are separate and only the first is automatable.
blocked_by: presenter_director is contract status PLANNED (build_order 7), NOT_PROVEN, autonomous_dispatch DISABLED
its enablement prerequisites are unmet and include an explicit human enablement decision by Mikko
PRODUCTION.human_owns: the physical performance itself, which no agent may synthesize away

MODE_UNSPECIFIED.detail: capture-checklist requires a declared production mode: its required evidence and owner differ between DRAFT, REVIEW, PRODUCTION

DRAFT.meaning: A zero-human draft cannot satisfy a gate that structurally requires a human approval marker placed after real capture evidence.
blocked_by: package-run-capture-evidence-review.js reaches PASS only with an exact human approval marker recorded after the evidence

rowHasRealCaptureEvidence explicitly rejects rows matching dummy, smoke-test, test-capture, test-screen, test-voiceover and generated checklist row, so synthetic capture cannot be presented as capture evidence
DRAFT.architecture_need: Either DRAFT needs a machine-verifiable proxy-capture disposition at gate 8, or the draft lifecycle must legitimately end before gate 8 and hand over to REVIEW. This is a human architecture decision, not a code fix, and it must not be resolved by weakening human gates generally.

REVIEW.meaning: Already settled by the run that produced the draft. Not re-evaluated because mode changed.

PRODUCTION.meaning: Mikko confirms the real captured material. This is the correct home for human capture authority, and it is why gate 7 should not ask for approval.
PRODUCTION.human_owns: confirmation that the captured material is what was intended
the physical performance itself, which no agent may synthesize away

owner_matrix.finding: The single GATE_OWNERS entry (presenter_director) is correct for PRODUCTION and wrong for DRAFT and REVIEW. A mode-aware owner projection is therefore needed, and the need is now proven rather than asserted.

live_evaluator_is_mode_blind.observed: The gate-7 evaluator returned NEEDS CAPTURE identically in the DRAFT and PRODUCTION canaries, with the same reason string.
live_evaluator_is_mode_blind.meaning: Gate 7 today cannot tell a proxy draft from a real recording session. That is the conflation, demonstrated rather than argued.

draft_mode_blockers: no synthetic delivery artifact contract: presenter-take-manifest models real human delivery only (TRANSCRIPT_SOURCES HUMAN_SUPPLIED/IMPORTED/EXTERNAL_TRANSCRIPTION, FIDELITY_METHODS including HUMAN_VERIFIED, createHumanSelection, verifyMediaBytes)
PRESENTER_A_ROLL is excluded from visual-plan-prompt-adapter PROMPT_MEDIA, so presenter delivery is contractually not machine-generable
no text-to-speech, avatar or synthetic-voice producer exists anywhere in the repository

gate 8 reaches PASS only with an exact human approval marker recorded after real capture evidence, and rowHasRealCaptureEvidence explicitly rejects dummy, smoke-test, test-capture, test-screen, test-voiceover and generated checklist row

review_mode_entry.finding: Gate 9 rough-cut-review is the natural Review Mode boundary: it is a HUMAN gate owned by editor and its artifacts are rough-cut-watch-notes.md and rough-cut-review.md — a human watching a produced draft.
review_mode_entry.caveat: A DRAFT run still cannot legitimately reach gate 9, because gate 8 sits between and requires human capture approval. Whether a draft should end before gate 8 or gain a machine proxy disposition at gate 8 is a human architecture decision.

lifecycle_orthogonality.proof: M10 asserts the full 14-gate order and position are byte-identical across DRAFT, REVIEW and PRODUCTION transitions; G7M10 asserts the policy cannot reorder, add or skip a gate.

retained_canary.policy: left unclassified deliberately. Guessing PRODUCTION would silently commit Mikko to a real performance; guessing DRAFT would silently claim a proxy is acceptable.

tests: M1-M14 run-mode contract, G7M1-G7M10 gate-7 policy, 21 total
verdict: DRAFT_MODE_BLOCKED_BY_CAPTURE_CONTRACT — the mode model is landed and proven; DRAFT cannot be satisfied by existing capabilities.
